# A round-up interval from two values of T

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `upward_make_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

The state of the round-up interval of two values of `T`, $[l_o, h_i]$ stored as $(h_i, -l_o)$; the whole line, $(+\infty, +\infty)$, when a bound is a NaN or both are the same infinity, and the empty set, both lanes a NaN, when they are reversed:

$$Z = [l_o, h_i].$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $Z$ as $(z_u, z_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $h_i$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$, stored as $(z_u, z_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval.
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other, or both are the same infinity ($[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the whole line, $(z_u, z_n) = (+\infty, +\infty)$.
- Otherwise, if the bounds are reversed, $l_o > h_i$ ($[+\infty, -\infty]$, and $l_o = +\infty$ or $h_i = -\infty$ with the other finite, among them): $Z$ is the empty set, both lanes a NaN.
- Otherwise ($l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$ and $h_i > -\infty$): $Z$ is $[l_o, h_i]$, $-z_n = l_o$ and $z_u = h_i$ as extended real numbers (a zero may change its sign).

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_make_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_make_1.kernel), the description the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) is generated from. The generator prints no C++ of it yet. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)). A line of two statements separated by ` | ` is a *pair line*: the two lanes of one instruction, lane 0 on the left ([the pair form](../developer/design/upward.md#the-pair-form)).

```
# An interval of the round-up interval from two values of T given by the program
# (docs/developer/design/upward.md, "Constructor and conversions"), with the cases of interval_make_1:
# the whole line (+inf, +inf) for a NaN bound and for the same infinity twice, the empty set (NaN, NaN)
# for reversed bounds, (hi, -lo) otherwise. No guard: the barrier on its inputs takes the place of
# rule R3 (rule U4). Interval(t) is this kernel on (t, t). Requires the rounding mode upward set by
# kairn::upward::Scope and the options of docs/concepts/upward.md (GCC and Clang -frounding-math,
# MSVC /fp:strict).

ok  = le(lo, hi)                                               # false with a NaN
nl  = lt(lo, const inf)
mi  = neg(const inf)
nu  = lt(mi, hi)
va  = and(ok, nl)
v   = and(va, nu)                                              # the pair describes an interval
rv  = lt(hi, lo)                                               # reversed; false with a NaN
nlo = neg(lo)
ou  = select(rv, const nan, const inf) | on = select(rv, const nan, const inf)   # rv broadcast
zu  = select(v, hi, ou)                | zn = select(v, nlo, on)                 # (hi, -lo): a make
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- What the compiled code gives where its environment is not the one of the statement: no flush to zero of results or operands (its result does not depend on the rounding mode). That is the program's to make so, as [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md#what-the-program-guarantees) says, and no proof covers that step ([What is not machine-checked](../concepts/correctness.md#what-is-not-machine-checked)).
